gaps.gap: No signed ULTRACODE / OWNER authorization artifact exists. The OWNER 2026-09-15 ULTRACODE directive text and DL number are not in decisions/ or the Vault (vault_contracts UNKNOWN); all six audits audit the contracts it WOULD amend, not the directive itself. Yet the integration touches three ROT-zone items: Company Structure hard-codes 'drei ... AIs' (a 4th AI seat is a structural change), and HR14/R4 are Hard Rules (a hard-rule change requires a DL + written OWNER approval per the Lessons-Learned Loop anti-pattern). It is also unresolved whether 'Kimi may author internal strategies' means a routable lane or an offline-only role feeding an existing seat — which determines whether any router change is even needed.
gaps.impact: Blocks legitimate start of ALL implementation. Building against un-written intent lets agents 'read intent' into a Hard Rule (exactly the HR14/R4 relaxation risk). Everything downstream is unauthorized until the directive is a dated decisions/ file naming: seat-vs-offline role, cost_rank, and the HR14/R4 EA-vs-research boundary.
gaps.how_to_close: Obtain the ULTRACODE directive as a dated immutable decisions/DL-NNN file that explicitly (a) grants/denies a routable Kimi seat, (b) states the EA-vs-research ML boundary preserving R4's in-EA reject list verbatim, (c) amends Company Structure 'drei AIs', and (d) fixes Kimi's cost_rank and pacing model. Confirm OWNER signature before any code/registry change.

gaps.gap: Kimi spend is a total governance blind spot. The CLI has NO usage/quota/limits subcommand (spend not programmatically queryable); the USD 99/mo subscription allowance, reset date, concurrency/rate-limit behavior are all UNKNOWN and untested. No KIMI governor lane, no KIMI_LOW_TOKENS-style flag, and the quota-governance contract names only Codex+Claude. An unthrottled AI seat directly violates the quota-governance contract.
gaps.impact: CRITICAL. A routed Kimi seat can silently exhaust the subscription or hit rate limits mid-pipeline with no pacing and no visibility, and the only budget-enforcement mechanism (weekly budget line + governor flags) cannot see it.
gaps.how_to_close: Design an external spend tracker (the status_line JSON snapshot exposes a 'usage' field on stdin — the only workaround) plus a governor lane and a router-side KIMI_DISABLED flag. First empirically characterize whether 'usage' is subscription-remaining vs per-session tokens, and probe parallel-call and rate-limit behavior.

gaps.gap: cost_rank for Kimi is unspecified and load-bearing, with a concrete capture failure mode. route_once orders eligible lanes by cost_rank ASC (gemini 10 / codex 20 / claude 30). The D10 code comment (agent_router.py) documents that because gemini declares [research,strategy] at the LOWEST cost_rank it captured EVERY research/strategy row — the weakest seat doing the hardest work. If Kimi is made routable via research/strategy and given a cost_rank below gemini's 10, it would capture all research/strategy AND the scalpel class the same way. No auditor stated what cost_rank Kimi should get.
gaps.impact: HIGH. Wrong cost_rank silently reroutes the entire research funnel (and possibly the scalpel-mechanization class) to an unproven, unpaced seat, bypassing existing tier contracts at the lane level.
gaps.how_to_close: OWNER/orchestrator must fix Kimi's cost_rank explicitly and decide which task_types it may claim. Prefer NEW task_types requiring the 8 Kimi-specific capabilities (so it is selectable only for intended work) over reusing research_strategy, and verify eligibility against _eligible_agents ordering before enabling the lane.

gaps.gap: Router-vs-execution pacing gap. A KIMI_LOW_QUOTA flag mirroring agy is read ONLY by agent_chain.vendor_gate/execution consumers, never by route_once. GATED_AGENTS = {codex, claude} (verified). So a Kimi flag alone paces the critic chain but NOT the deterministic router — the router keeps dispatching Kimi orchestration tickets while nominally 'paced'.
gaps.impact: HIGH. Kimi can appear throttled yet keep routing and spending. This is the same trap that required the claude-style CLAUDE_DISABLED router disable.
gaps.how_to_close: Add Kimi to GATED_AGENTS or add a claude-style KIMI_DISABLED handling in sync_default_registry so the router disables the lane, in addition to any vendor_gate flag.

gaps.gap: Execution-adapter behavior is almost entirely untested (one 6.2s call, exit 0 only). UNKNOWN: whether kimi -p reads a piped prompt from stdin vs only argv (~32KB Windows cmdline limit, no --prompt-file — research prompts are large); stdin vs TTY/ConPTY (agy-class silent hang-to-timeout); stream-json event framing (parser undesigned); non-zero exit-code taxonomy (no robust error handling possible); no CLI timeout flag (needs external watchdog); malformed argv drops into the interactive TUI (headless hang). Text output is dirty (version banner + thinking bullets + resume trailer) so naive stdout capture fails.
gaps.impact: HIGH. Any of these can hang a slot to timeout or silently corrupt captured research output. An adapter cannot be built robustly without empirically characterizing them.
gaps.how_to_close: Run a short controlled probe battery (read-only-safe): stream-json framing, stdin-vs-argv prompt delivery, deliberate error to map exit codes, and a malformed-argv guard. Design the adapter on stream-json (not text), bound every call with an external watchdog, and default MaxSessions=1.

gaps.gap: Auth is a short-lived (900s) rolling token dependent on refresh; the credential file is a plain-JSON file owned by qm-admin, world-readable but qm-admin-writable. Scheduled tasks run as SYSTEM (session 0). If a SYSTEM-run Kimi orchestration must WRITE a refreshed token it may lack write permission (needs the run_in_console_session.ps1 hop used by agy/gemini), and a shared single credential file across concurrent processes is a Codex-class refresh race that can invalidate the login.
gaps.impact: HIGH. Silent auth failure under the scheduled-task identity, or a token race that logs Kimi out (requiring interactive kimi login, not headlessly automatable except via kimi acp --login).
gaps.how_to_close: icacls-check the credential file ACL for SYSTEM write; route Kimi orchestration through the console-session hop like agy if auth is user-bound; keep MaxSessions=1 until per-session auth isolation is proven; monitor token-refresh failures.

gaps.gap: The internal R1 QM-RESEARCH source contract has no resolver/store and a concrete false-reject blocker. QM-RESEARCH://<id> exists nowhere (no path/format/content-addressing). card_intake_prescreen._affirmative_prohibited_mechanics scans the WHOLE card text for ML terms (verified line 483/541) — an internal-research card describing ML-derived provenance in affirmative prose is tagged PROHIBITED_MECHANICS:ML and moved to cards_rejected on --apply. VALID_SOURCE_TYPES is a fixed 8-tuple excluding internal_research and add-source rejects others (verified). Identifier form (AI-KIMI-... vs QM-RESEARCH://) unspecified; six-section charter-check applicability to internal cards UNKNOWN.
gaps.impact: HIGH. Kimi-authored cards get auto-rejected at prescreen, and there is no durable content-addressed store — recreating the agy-video hallucination-as-source failure mode the org explicitly guards against.
gaps.how_to_close: Scope the prescreen ML scan to the mechanics section (or exempt a declared provenance section); decide DB-row vs card+decisions-only lane (extend VALID_SOURCE_TYPES only if a routable DB row is wanted); reserve an AI-KIMI-/QM-RESEARCH- namespace with mandatory source_author + source_sha256; store the artifact in-repo on C: (strategy-seeds/sources/) with the sha256 authority recorded in an immutable decisions/ receipt.

gaps.gap: HR14 (Vault, blanket 'alles verboten', EA-agnostic) lags the repo, where R4 is already 'narrowed to ML-only' (qb_reputable_source_criteria.md:19) and EA-runtime-scoped (build_check scans only .mq5/.mqh). ULTRACODE's 'ML allowed offline in research' has no signed annex reconciling these two surfaces, and Determinism-Over-LLM-Calls binds any offline ML to terminate in mechanical rules + a durable auditable artifact.
gaps.impact: MEDIUM-HIGH. Without an explicit annexed EA-vs-research boundary that preserves R4's in-EA reject list verbatim, an agent can justify PnL-adaptive/online-learning logic by 'intent'. The two ML surfaces (Vault HR14 vs repo R4) can also drift further.
gaps.how_to_close: Annex HR14 and R4 with the EA-vs-research boundary, keep R4's in-EA list (neural nets/ONNX/PnL-adaptive/online-retrain) unchanged, and require every offline-ML research output to reduce to mechanical rules + a durable artifact per Determinism-Over-LLM-Calls.

gaps.gap: The pre-Q00 edge-discovery layer has no experiment-memory / search-history ledger, and Kimi's hypothesis volume is not connected to DSR multiple-testing correction. The dsr_cohort/v1 schema already REQUIRES search_history + declared/selection/research/effective trial_count, but no populated store exists. If Kimi generates many offline hypotheses without logging trial counts into the DSR path, survivorship/DSR is uncorrectable. Also: the research Python env is bare (numpy only; pandas/scipy/sklearn/duckdb missing), offline wheel resolution untested; D: has only ~65 GB free (below the 60 GB live purge line's headroom and the 150 GB no-op line) so research intermediates on D: risk tripping DISK_MIN_FREE_GB=40 and stalling backtests.
gaps.impact: MEDIUM-HIGH. Uncounted trials silently inflate DSR-based survivorship (a scientific-integrity failure); an uncontrolled research job can starve the MT5 workers that are the primary throughput metric.
gaps.how_to_close: Design a NEW append-only versioned JSONL search-history ledger (mirroring tester_memory_ledger.jsonl) that feeds trial_count into dsr_cohort; build an isolated uv venv (never pip into Python311); land research outputs small and on C:/G:, and gate the research process on the same worker CPU/RAM latches at low priority.

gaps.gap: Cross-vendor critic integration is undesigned for Kimi, and the 'research critic' capability is unexecutable today. run_seat's vendor switch is hardcoded claude/codex/agy and raises ChainError on unknown vendors (verified agent_chain.v1.json vendors = claude/codex/agy, cross_vendor_required true, no kimi key). A Kimi-created artifact would fall to the 'unknown' creator bucket (non-kimi critics — structurally OK), but Kimi can never BE a critic without a vendor block + by_creator_vendor candidacy + VENDOR_ALIASES + run_kimi adapter. Whether Kimi may be a SOLE critic is undecided (agy is explicitly backup-only, 'halluziniert').
gaps.impact: MEDIUM. The requested 'research critic' capability cannot run; and giving Kimi critic authority without deciding sole-critic eligibility repeats the agy quality risk.
gaps.how_to_close: If Kimi is to critique, add the full vendor block/adapter and an explicit allow-sole-critic decision (mirror the allow_agy gate); if not, keep Kimi creator-only and REVIEW-terminal so run_seat is never asked to dispatch it.

contradictions: Integration-mechanism fork, unreconciled: kimi_cli calls the ACP-over-stdio server (`kimi acp`) 'the most robust programmatic integration path', while router_providers designs entirely around per-agent one-shot CLI branches (resolve_cli/command_for/run_kimi using `kimi -p`). The two auditors propose different execution substrates and neither reconciles which the farm should adopt — a foundational design decision left open.

Template-seat state is itself unresolved: vault_contracts treats agy/Antigravity as research-only per the routing contract, but drift shows the LIVE registry gemini(=agy) lane declares code/tests/repo_edit and the orchestration prompt lets it draft code (an in-code comment says this is a 'SEPARATE OWNER decision ... Leave the rest exactly as-is'). router_providers proposes copying agy's patterns for Kimi — so the design copies a seat whose own capability scope is an open OWNER question, propagating the ambiguity.

Kimi token 'validity' is point-in-time only: kimi_cli reports the access token 'valid at audit time' (expires_at 2026-09-15T09:57:48Z), but at my read (2026-09-15T09:58:02Z) the on-disk token had already expired (~14s prior), confirming a rolling 900s token refreshed only on invocation, not a stable credential — the summary's 'valid' should not be read as durable.

Surface-agreement fragility: vault_contracts stresses the code registry beats the Vault table and they currently AGREE on four seats; but the same audit notes CLAUDE.md prose, the routing-contract table, and DEFAULT_AGENT_REGISTRY are three separate surfaces. A partial Kimi add (any one surface without DEFAULT_AGENT_REGISTRY + agent_chain vendor block + a quota flag) leaves Kimi either non-existent as a lane or unthrottled — the auditors agree it's a risk but no single owner of 'all surfaces updated atomically' is named.
